text:
maya: Nightly eval flagged a regression after promptpack v41 landed. overall macro F1 dropped 3.4% on pset_punct, and the failure mode looks focused on punctuation-heavy examples (quotes, em-dashes, soft hyphens). attaching diff and a couple failing samples. https://ci.internal/reports/1728001234

maya: diff: `pset/promptpack_v40 -> v41` shows we removed a canonical example with weird punctuation and tightened example wording. not sure if the change amplified tokenization edge cases.

maya: failing sample (input):
```
Customer: "I need the total—incl. tax and shipping—by 3/31. Soft‑hyphen details in the SKU: ABCD
Format: table
```
expected: table with 4 rows
actual: generator splits SKU and drops hyphen, merges cells, returns prose.

eval-bot: nightly-eval: alert for pset_punct: delta F1 -3.4% (p<0.01). Top regressions: punctuation-split, SKU-tokenize, numeric-extraction. Link: https://ci.internal/nightly/1728001234

sam: Is this likely a prompt wording regress or tokenizer quirks? v41 also included the small tokenizer update ONNX-qtz.

li: I checked token diffs for that sample — token boundaries changed where we removed the canonical example. soft-hyphen (U+00AD) is being normalized away by the new canonical example processing rule. so it's a promptset-change -> tokenization interaction.

sam: ah ok - so it's not quantization. can we repro locally with pset_v41 + current tokenizer? if yes we should either revert the prompt wording or rebaseline with a tiny patch to canonical examples.

maya: repro steps I ran:
```
git checkout promptpack/v41
python -m eval.run --pset pset_punct --samples 500 --model rwd-12b
# observe token boundary on sample 234
```
I can push a minimal patch that escapes or adds the canonical punctuation example back.

julian: If it's just the removed canonical example causing distribution shift, I'd lean rebaseline instead of rollback if we can get approvals quickly. What's the cost of a rebaseline?

li: Rebaseline checklist: update promptpack metadata, run canary eval (10k samples), run smoke on dedicated, bump pset version and record delta. Time: ~2-3h for canary + 1h for approvals. We should also add a unit test for soft-hyphen cases.

sam: I'm fine with rebaseline if diff is small. can we get sign-off from product on whether that canonical example is still valuable? julian, tagging you for rapid approval. @julian

julian: 👍 please attach the proposed change (PR link) and the canary results. if the canary passes and delta is within tolerance after adding a targeted test, approve rebaseline.

maya: created PR: https://git.internal/promptpack/pulls/3278 - short description: "restore punct example; add soft-hyphen unit test". includes proposed changelog and eval script. requesting canary run now.

eval-bot: canary-run started (canary-cluster-dedicated). run id: canary-1728001234-1

li: quick note: also adding a tokenizer normalization guard in the prompt preprocessor to preserve visible control chars for psets marked as "sensitive-punct". I'll include in the PR as opt-in.

sam: thanks. will wait for canary. if it fails we revert the promptpack change and open a follow-up to audit other removed canonical examples.

eval-bot: canary-run finished. metrics: pset_punct delta F1 +0.2% vs v40 baseline (n=10k). regressions resolved for top-10 failure cases. details: https://ci.internal/canary/canary-1728001234-1

maya: canary looks good. requesting approval from julian for rebaseline merge.

julian: Approved. merging PR now. :merge: :rocket:

sam: cheers. can we add a post-merge job to scan for other canonical-example removals that touch punctuation? might save another morning triage.

li: will add a lint rule to flag removals that match regex for punctuation-heavy examples. queued in infra backlog.

maya: thanks all — will monitor nightly and keep an eye for any remaining soft-hyphen surprises. :mag:

julian: great job catching the narrow failure mode early.
